text:
alyssa: Quick proposal — build a tiny "package-concierge" CLI operators run on bastions for air-gapped upgrades. It mediates between operator media (USB/NFS) or a one-way mirror and the node-local seed-agent. Goals: low operator friction, offline-first security, resumable transfers, and clear audit artifacts.

ben: sounds promising. is this meant to replace seed-agent?

alyssa: adjunct. seed-agent remains the on-node enforcer for activation semantics. concierge is ephemeral, UX-focused, and never holds signing keys. It only verifies signed manifests and streams blobs to seed-agent.

carlos: primary concern: metadata leakage. concierge must not phone home. default should be completely offline unless operator explicitly enables mirror fetch.

diana: agreed. propose two modes: `offline-ingest` (no outbound) and `mirror-proxy` (operator-provided mirror URL; outbound allowed only from concierge). Telemetry off by default and opt-in via explicit env/flag.

alyssa: proposed flow:
1) concierge validates manifest signature locally using operator-provided trust roots
2) concierge streams content in chunked, resumable fashion to seed-agent over mTLS
3) seed-agent stages chunks to a staging area, verifies checksums and signatures, associates a monotonic manifest id
4) operator triggers `seed-agent activate --manifest-id X` which runs activation window and atomically flips the activation pointer if checks pass

ben: how to avoid partial activations on transfer failure?

carlos: seed-agent staging + atomic pointer swap. Provide an `apply-token` that concierge can request so resumed uploads are tied to a staging record. If activate fails, activate can roll back to previous pointer.

alyssa: UX and CLI sketches:

```
# validate + stage from attached media
redwood-concierge ingest --source /mnt/usb --manifest /mnt/usb/redwood.json --target 10.0.0.5:8443 --verify

# resume a failed ingest
redwood-concierge resume --token abc123 --target 10.0.0.5:8443

# mirror mode (one-way mirror)
redwood-concierge mirror --manifest https://mirror.local/redwood.json --allow-outbound --target 10.0.0.5:8443

# dry-run to estimate size
redwood-concierge dry-run --manifest /mnt/usb/redwood.json
```

diana: security: concierge runs as operator user, seed-agent as system service. Require one-time registration token (displayed on admin console) to bind concierge to the node. Use mTLS with short-lived certs. Concierge must support multiple trust roots and reject ambiguous manifests.

carlos: storage semantics: staging must be copy-on-write with refcounts. Keep previous image until activate completes. Rollback is `activate --previous` which repoints the activation pointer after quick health checks.

ben: failure modes: what if operator disconnects during activate? seed-agent should use an activation lease. After lease expiry, either auto-rollback or require manual reconciliation. Also provide an operator-signed audit record JSON that concierge writes and seed-agent stores.

alyssa: performance knobs: conservative defaults (parallel fetch up to 4, dedupe enabled). Provide `--unsafe-fast` for more aggressive parallelism and `--dry-run`. Also `--simulate-fail-after N` for CI tests.

infra-bot: TODO: add unit tests for resume and integration test for `concierge --simulate-fail-after N-chunks` to exercise idempotency.

open questions for reviewers:
- registration UX: token vs QR vs one-time file
- chunking policy: fixed 4MB vs adaptive based on RTT/bandwidth
- whether concierge should automatically re-stream from mirror after a failed staging attempt or require explicit `resume`

diana: my preferences: token + QR for convenience, adaptive chunking based on latency, allow re-stream only after seed-agent signals `resume-allowed`.

ben: +1 adaptive chunking, add a `perf-mode` toggle.

carlos: +1 token/QR, keep logs verbose by default and ensure `--dry-run` exists for approvals.

alyssa: I'll write a short RFC with diagrams, syscall-level notes (umask, secure tmpdir, chroot option), and a `diagnostic` mode for verbose logs to include in support bundles. Will link RFC in #architecture and tag reviewers once ready. :thumbsup:
